learn.b: Japanese uses three scripts: hiragana, katakana and kanji. Hiragana is the first one to learn. It has 46 basic sounds, and each character is one beat. The five vowels are あ (a), い (i), う (u), え (e), お (o).
K row: か (ka) き (ki) く (ku) け (ke) こ (ko). S row: さ (sa) し (shi) す (su) せ (se) そ (so). T row: た (ta) ち (chi) つ (tsu) て (te) と (to). N row: な (na) に (ni) ぬ (nu) ね (ne) の (no).
Read from left to right, one character at a time. かさ (kasa) means umbrella and has 2 beats. さかな (sakana) means fish and has 3 beats. The sound ん (n) is a beat on its own.

qs.q: Which hiragana sounds like 'ku'?
qs.why: く is ku. け is ke, こ is ko and き is ki.

qs.q: How do you read し?
qs.why: し is read 'shi', the second sound of the S row.

qs.q: Which row does の (no) belong to?
qs.why: な に ぬ ね の make the N row.

qs.q: How many beats does さかな (sakana) have?
qs.why: sa-ka-na is three beats.

qs.q: つ is read 'tsu'.
qs.why: つ belongs to the T row and is read 'tsu'.

learn.b: H row: は (ha) ひ (hi) ふ (fu) へ (he) ほ (ho). M row: ま (ma) み (mi) む (mu) め (me) も (mo). Y row: や (ya) ゆ (yu) よ (yo). R row: ら (ra) り (ri) る (ru) れ (re) ろ (ro). Also わ (wa), を (o) and ん (n). As a particle, は is read 'wa'.
Add two dots (dakuten) to change a sound: か (ka) becomes が (ga), さ (sa) becomes ざ (za), た (ta) becomes だ (da), は (ha) becomes ば (ba). Add a small circle (handakuten) to は to make ぱ (pa).
A small ゃ ゅ ょ joins the sound before it: き (ki) + ゃ makes きゃ (kya), and し + ゅ makes しゅ (shu). A small っ doubles the next consonant: きって (kitte) means stamp.

qs.q: Which hiragana sounds like 'ha'?
qs.why: は is ha. ほ is ho, ま is ma and わ is wa.

qs.q: What sound do you get when you add two dots to か (ka)?
qs.why: か with two dots is が (ga).

qs.q: Which mark turns は (ha) into ぱ (pa)?
qs.why: The small circle (handakuten) makes a 'p' sound.

qs.q: How do you read きゃ?
qs.why: きゃ is one beat, read 'kya'.

qs.q: A small っ makes the next consonant sound double, as in きって (kitte).
qs.why: The small っ adds a short pause before the next consonant.

learn.b: Katakana is the second script. It is used for foreign words, foreign names and sounds. It has the same sounds as hiragana but with sharper shapes: ア (a) イ (i) ウ (u) エ (e) オ (o), カ (ka) キ (ki) ク (ku) ケ (ke) コ (ko), サ (sa) シ (shi) ス (su) セ (se) ソ (so).

タ (ta) チ (chi) ツ (tsu) テ (te) ト (to), ナ (na) ニ (ni) ヌ (nu) ネ (ne) ノ (no), ハ (ha) ヒ (hi) フ (fu) ヘ (he) ホ (ho), マ (ma) ミ (mi) ム (mu), ラ (ra) リ (ri) ル (ru), ン (n). A long line ー makes the vowel long. Dots and circles work as in hiragana.
コーヒー (koohii) is coffee. テレビ (terebi) is TV. ホテル (hoteru) is hotel. ピザ (piza) is pizza. ハンバーガー (hanbaagaa) is hamburger. Names like ケン (Ken) are also written in katakana.

qs.q: Which script is used for foreign words like コーヒー?
qs.why: Foreign loanwords are normally written in katakana.

qs.q: What does コーヒー (koohii) mean?

qs.q: Which katakana is read 'shi'?
qs.why: シ is shi. ツ is tsu, ソ is so and ン is n.

qs.q: What does the long mark ー do?
o: It makes the vowel before it long
qs.why: ー stretches the previous vowel, as in コーヒー (koohii).

qs.q: ピザ (piza) is normally written in hiragana.
qs.why: Foreign words such as ピザ are written in katakana.

learn.b: こんにちは (konnichiwa) means hello. おはよう (ohayou) is good morning, and こんばんは (konbanwa) is good evening. Use them at different times of the day.
ありがとう (arigatou) means thank you. すみません (sumimasen) means excuse me or sorry. さようなら (sayounara) means goodbye.
Say はじめまして (hajimemashite) when you meet someone. Then say わたしは ○○ です (watashi wa ○○ desu), which means I am ○○.

learn.b: ごはん (gohan) is rice or a meal. さかな (sakana) is fish and にく (niku) is meat. りんご (ringo) is apple and パン (pan) is bread.
みず (mizu) is water and おちゃ (ocha) is tea. たべます (tabemasu) means eat and のみます (nomimasu) means drink.
おいしい (oishii) means delicious. すき (suki) means like. ください (kudasai) means please give me.

learn.b: です (desu) is like am, is, or are. Add か (ka) at the end to make a question. がっこうですか (gakkou desu ka) means Is it school?
Polite verbs end in ます (masu). いきます (ikimasu) means go, きます (kimasu) means come, and みます (mimasu) means see or watch.
Change ます (masu) to ません (masen) for no. たべません (tabemasen) means do not eat. Use います (imasu) for living things and あります (arimasu) for objects.

qs.why: か (ka) turns a sentence into a question.

qs.q: What does いきます (ikimasu) mean?

learn.b: Add じ (ji) to a number for o'clock: いちじ (ichiji) is 1:00, にじ (niji) 2:00, さんじ (sanji) 3:00. Careful: 4:00 is よじ (yoji), 7:00 is しちじ (shichiji) and 9:00 is くじ (kuji). はん (han) means half. ごぜん (gozen) is AM and ごご (gogo) is PM.
にちようび (nichiyoubi) is Sunday, げつようび (getsuyoubi) Monday, かようび (kayoubi) Tuesday, すいようび (suiyoubi) Wednesday, もくようび (mokuyoubi) Thursday, きんようび (kinyoubi) Friday, どようび (doyoubi) Saturday.
きょう (kyou) is today, あした (ashita) is tomorrow and きのう (kinou) is yesterday. Use に (ni) after a time: しちじに おきます (shichiji ni okimasu) means I get up at 7. ねます (nemasu) means sleep.

qs.why: しちじ is 7:00, に marks the time and おきます means get up.

qs.why: ごぜん is AM and ごご is PM.

learn.b: Many adjectives end in い: おおきい (ookii) big, ちいさい (chiisai) small, あたらしい (atarashii) new, ふるい (furui) old, あつい (atsui) hot, さむい (samui) cold. They go before the noun: おおきい いぬ (ookii inu) is a big dog. For no, change い to くない: おおきくない (ookikunai).

Some adjectives need な before a noun: きれい (kirei) pretty or clean, しずか (shizuka) quiet, げんき (genki) healthy. きれいな はな (kirei na hana) is a pretty flower. For no, use じゃ ありません: しずかじゃ ありません (shizuka ja arimasen).

あかい (akai) is red, あおい (aoi) is blue, しろい (shiroi) is white and くろい (kuroi) is black. とても (totemo) means very. これ (kore) means this: これは とても おもしろい です (kore wa totemo omoshiroi desu) means This is very interesting.

qs.why: ちいさい means small.

o: おおきじゃ ありません (ookiji ja arimasen)
qs.why: For い-adjectives, drop い and add くない.

qs.q: Which word is a な-adjective?
qs.why: きれい ends in い but is a な-adjective.

きれいの はな (kirei no hana)

learn.b: Particles are small words after nouns. は (wa) marks the topic. を (o) marks the object. に (ni) shows a direction or time. で (de) shows where an action happens. の (no) shows belonging. も (mo) means also. Remember: は is read 'wa' and を is read 'o'.
うち (uchi) is home, えき (eki) station, みせ (mise) shop, こうえん (kouen) park. がっこうに いきます (gakkou ni ikimasu) means I go to school. レストランで たべます (resutoran de tabemasu) means I eat at a restaurant.
わたしの ほん (watashi no hon) means my book. うえ (ue) is on or above, した (shita) is under and なか (naka) is inside. ほんは つくえの うえに あります (hon wa tsukue no ue ni arimasu) means The book is on the desk.

qs.why: を marks what the verb acts on.

learn.b: Change ます (masu) to ました (mashita) for the past. たべます (tabemasu) becomes たべました (tabemashita), which means ate.
Use ませんでした (masen deshita) for did not. いきませんでした (ikimasen deshita) means did not go. The past of です (desu) is でした (deshita).
きのう (kinou) means yesterday. けさ (kesa) means this morning. These words often come near the start of the sentence.

learn.b: ru-verbs: drop る and add て: たべる becomes たべて (tabete). Irregular: する becomes して (shite), くる becomes きて (kite). u-verbs: う/つ/る become って (かう becomes かって), む/ぶ/ぬ become んで (のむ becomes のんで), く becomes いて (かく becomes かいて), す becomes して (はなす becomes はなして). いく is special: いって (itte).

Verb in te-form + ください (kudasai) means please do. ちょっと まって ください (chotto matte kudasai) means Please wait a moment. ゆっくり はなして ください (yukkuri hanashite kudasai) means Please speak slowly. Add もいいですか (mo ii desu ka) to ask for permission.

Te-form + います (imasu) means is doing: べんきょうして います (benkyou shite imasu) is I am studying. The te-form also links actions: あさ おきて、ごはんを たべます (asa okite, gohan o tabemasu) means I get up, then eat breakfast.

qs.q: What is the te-form of たべる (taberu)?
qs.why: For ru-verbs drop る and add て.

qs.q: What is the te-form of のむ (nomu)?
qs.why: む-verbs become んで.

qs.q: What does ゆっくり はなして ください mean?
qs.why: ゆっくり is slowly and はなして is from はなす, to speak.

qs.why: Te-form + います shows an ongoing action.

びょういん (byouin) is hospital and ぎんこう (ginkou) is bank. ちかい (chikai) means near and とおい (tooi) means far.

learn.b: でんしゃ (densha) is train and ひこうき (hikouki) is airplane. きっぷ (kippu) is ticket. りょこう (ryokou) means trip.
いくらですか (ikura desu ka) means How much is it? たかい (takai) means expensive or high. やすい (yasui) means cheap.
Use ○○が ほしいです (○○ ga hoshii desu) for I want ○○. きっぷが ほしいです (kippu ga hoshii desu) means I want a ticket.

qs.why: いくら (ikura) means how much.

qs.why: でんしゃ (densha) means train.

learn.b: With friends and family, Japanese uses plain form. The dictionary form is the plain present: たべます becomes たべる (taberu), のみます becomes のむ (nomu), いきます becomes いく (iku), します becomes する (suru), きます becomes くる (kuru).

Plain negative ends in ない: たべない (tabenai), のまない (nomanai), いかない (ikanai), しない (shinai), こない (konai). Plain past of ru-verbs is た: たべた (tabeta). For のむ it is のんだ (nonda). Past negative: たべなかった (tabenakatta).

Drop か and use a rising voice for questions: ごはん たべた? (gohan tabeta?) Yes is うん (un) and no is ううん (uun). Casual です is だ (da): がくせいだ (gakusei da). The い-adjective past is かった: おいしかった (oishikatta) was delicious.

learn.b: Kanji are characters from China. Each has a meaning and often two readings. Days use them: 日 (nichi, hi) is sun or day, 月 (getsu, tsuki) is moon or month, 火 (ka, hi) is fire, 水 (sui, mizu) is water, 木 (moku, ki) is tree, 金 (kin) is gold, 土 (do, tsuchi) is earth.

人 (hito, jin) is person. 大 (ookii, dai) is big and 小 (chiisai, shou) is small. 中 (naka, chuu) is middle or inside. 山 (yama) is mountain, 川 (kawa) is river and 口 (kuchi) is mouth. Many look like pictures of the thing.

Kanji combine into words. 日本 (nihon) is Japan: sun + origin. 本 (hon) means book. 日本人 (nihonjin) is a Japanese person. 学 (gaku) means study and 生 (sei) means life, so 学生 (gakusei) is student. 学校 (gakkou) is school.

learn.b: Pinyin writes Mandarin sounds with the Roman alphabet. A syllable has an initial (the start) and a final (the rest), plus a tone. Initials: b p m f, d t n l, g k h, j q x, zh ch sh r, z c s. Finals: a o e i u ü, ai ei ao ou, an en ang eng, ong.

q sounds like 'ch' in cheese with spread lips. x is like 'sh' with a smile. zh is like 'j' in jam with the tongue curled back. c is like 'ts' in cats and z is like 'ds' in beds. ü is said with round lips while saying 'ee'.
b, d, g are soft. p, t, k puff out air: bā and pā sound different. After j, q, x the letter u is really ü, so 去 (qù) has the ü sound. Examples: 你 (nǐ), 好 (hǎo), 学 (xué).

learn.h: Four tones and a light tone
learn.b: Tone 1 is high and flat: mā (妈, mother). Tone 2 rises: má (麻, hemp). Tone 3 dips down and up: mǎ (马, horse). Tone 4 falls sharply: mà (骂, scold). A neutral tone is short and light: ma. The mark goes on the vowel; if there is a, it takes it.
When two third tones are together, the first one is said as a second tone. So 你好 (nǐ hǎo) is said ní hǎo. It is still written nǐ hǎo. Say it aloud and it feels natural.
不 (bù) becomes bú before a fourth tone: 不是 (bú shì). 一 (yī) becomes yí before a fourth tone: 一个 (yí gè). Before tones 1, 2 and 3 it becomes yì: 一天 (yì tiān).

qs.why: The 4th tone drops from high to low, like mà.

learn.b: In Chinese you put a measure word between a number and a noun. 一个人 (yí gè rén) means one person. 个 (gè) is the most common and works for many things.

For two things use 两 (liǎng), not 二: 两个人 (liǎng gè rén). To ask how many, use 几 (jǐ): 你有几个哥哥? (nǐ yǒu jǐ gè gēge) means How many older brothers do you have?

月 (yuè) means month and 号 (hào) means day of the month: 十月五号 (shí yuè wǔ hào) is October 5th. 年 (nián) means year. Time words go before the verb: 我明天去学校 (wǒ míngtiān qù xuéxiào) means I go to school tomorrow.

learn.b: Add 吗 (ma) at the end of a statement. 你是学生吗? (nǐ shì xuéshēng ma?) means Are you a student? To answer, repeat the verb: 是 (shì) for yes, 不是 (bú shì) for no.

什么 (shénme) is what, 谁 (shéi) is who, 哪儿 (nǎr) is where, 几 (jǐ) is how many, 怎么 (zěnme) is how and 为什么 (wèishénme) is why. The question word stays where the answer would go: 你吃什么? (nǐ chī shénme?) means What do you eat? 这 (zhè) is this and 那 (nà) is that: 这是什么? means What is this?
呢 (ne) asks back: 我很好，你呢? (wǒ hěn hǎo, nǐ ne?) means I am fine, and you? Verb + 不 + verb asks a choice: 你去不去? (nǐ qù bú qù?) means Are you going or not?

learn.b: Adjectives do not need 是. Put 很 (hěn) before them: 我很高 (wǒ hěn gāo) means I am tall. Not 我是高. Useful: 大 (dà) big, 小 (xiǎo) small, 好 (hǎo) good, 高 (gāo) tall, 新 (xīn) new, 漂亮 (piàoliang) pretty, 热 (rè) hot, 冷 (lěng) cold.
的 (de) links an owner or a description to a noun. 我的书 (wǒ de shū) means my book. 好看的书 (hǎokàn de shū) means a good-looking book. For close family you can drop it: 我妈妈 (wǒ māma).
红 (hóng) is red, 白 (bái) is white, 黑 (hēi) is black and 蓝 (lán) is blue. Add 色 (sè) for color: 红色 (hóngsè). 红色的苹果 (hóngsè de píngguǒ) means a red apple. 不 makes it negative: 我不高 (wǒ bù gāo).

learn.b: Put 了 (le) after a verb to show an action is done. 我吃了 (wǒ chī le) means I ate. 昨天 (zuótiān) means yesterday.
Put 过 (guo) after a verb to say you have done it before. 我去过中国 (wǒ qù guo Zhōngguó) means I have been to China.
Use 没 (méi) to say you did not do something. 我没吃饭 (wǒ méi chī fàn) means I did not eat. Do not add 了 (le) after it.

learn.b: Put 在 (zài) before a verb for an action in progress: 我在吃饭 (wǒ zài chī fàn) means I am eating. 正在 (zhèngzài) is stronger: 他正在看书 (tā zhèngzài kàn shū). The negative is 没在 (méi zài).
Duration goes after the verb and 了, before the object: 我学了两年中文 (wǒ xué le liǎng nián Zhōngwén) means I studied Chinese for two years. 小时 (xiǎoshí) means hour: 我看了一个小时 (wǒ kàn le yí gè xiǎoshí).
着 (zhe) shows a continuing state: 门开着 (mén kāi zhe) means The door is open. 要…了 (yào…le) shows something is about to happen: 火车要来了 (huǒchē yào lái le) means The train is about to come.

learn.b: A second word after a verb shows the result: 看懂 (kàndǒng) means read and understand, 听懂 (tīngdǒng) listen and understand, 看见 (kànjiàn) see, 吃完 (chīwán) finish eating, 做好 (zuòhǎo) get done. Negative: 我没看懂 (wǒ méi kàndǒng) means I did not understand.
来 (lái) and 去 (qù) show direction: 进来 (jìnlái) is come in, 出去 (chūqù) is go out, 回来 (huílái) is come back and 回去 (huíqù) is go back. 来 moves toward the speaker and 去 moves away.
Verb + 得 (de) + adjective says how an action is done: 他说得很好 (tā shuō de hěn hǎo) means He speaks well. 她跑得很快 (tā pǎo de hěn kuài) means She runs fast. With an object, repeat the verb: 他说中文说得很好.

生病 (shēngbìng) means to get sick. 感冒 (gǎnmào) is a cold and 发烧 (fāshāo) is a fever. 医生 (yīshēng) is a doctor and 药 (yào) is medicine. 看病 (kànbìng) means to see a doctor. 不舒服 (bù shūfu) means not feeling well.
应该 (yīnggāi) means should: 你应该休息 (nǐ yīnggāi xiūxi) means You should rest. 多喝水 (duō hē shuǐ) means drink more water. 别 (bié) means don't: 别担心 (bié dānxīn) means Don't worry.

learn.b: 把 (bǎ) moves the object before the verb to show what you do to it. Pattern: subject + 把 + object + verb + extra. 我把书放在桌子上 (wǒ bǎ shū fàng zài zhuōzi shang) means I put the book on the table. 放 (fàng) is put and 桌子 (zhuōzi) is table.
The verb cannot stand alone: add 了, a complement or a place. 我把作业做完了 (wǒ bǎ zuòyè zuò wán le) means I finished my homework. 作业 (zuòyè) is homework. The object should be known or specific.

Put 没 and modal words before 把: 我没把门关好 (wǒ méi bǎ mén guān hǎo) means I did not close the door properly. 请把门关上 (qǐng bǎ mén guān shàng) means Please close the door. 关 (guān) is close and 开 (kāi) is open.

我把作业做完了 (wǒ bǎ zuòyè zuò wán le)
我做把作业完了 (wǒ zuò bǎ zuòyè wán le)
qs.why: The verb needs a result such as 完了.

qs.why: 没 goes before 把.

qs.q: A 把 sentence usually needs a result or extra word after the verb.
qs.why: The verb cannot stand alone.

learn.b: 先…再… (xiān…zài…) means first…then: 先吃饭，再去学校. 一边…一边… (yìbiān…yìbiān…) means doing two things at once: 一边吃饭一边看电视 (yìbiān chī fàn yìbiān kàn diànshì).
还是 (háishi) means or in questions: 你喝茶还是咖啡? (nǐ hē chá háishi kāfēi?) means Do you drink tea or coffee? 或者 (huòzhě) means or in statements: 我喝茶或者咖啡 (wǒ hē chá huòzhě kāfēi).

learn.b: Many characters have a radical that hints at meaning. 氵 means water: 河 (hé) is river. 口 means mouth: 吃 (chī) is eat and 喝 (hē) is drink. 亻 means person: 你 (nǐ) is you and 他 (tā) is he.

女 means woman: 妈 (mā), 姐 (jiě), and 好 (hǎo) is woman + child. 木 is tree: 林 (lín) forest has two trees and 森 (sēn) has three. 日 (sun) + 月 (moon) make 明 (míng), bright. 钅 means metal: 钱 (qián) is money.

Write strokes from top to bottom and from left to right. Mainland China uses simplified characters, for example 马 instead of 馬 and 学 instead of 學. Count strokes: 一 has 1, 人 has 2, 大 has 3 and 水 has 4.

qs.q: What is the general stroke order rule?

qs.why: Most characters follow top-to-bottom, left-to-right.

qs.why: Simplified characters have fewer strokes.
